title: Television shows that employed jazz musicians
summary: Willard notes the hidden work of jazz players on network shows, and Callender lists Danny Kaye, Jonathan Winters, Carol Burnett and Flip Wilson, twelve years of live shows.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I just think it's interesting, and not many people away from the West Coast or the two Coasts realize how many really major Jazz musicians make their living, or used to when there were more bands on television, facelessly on the network television shows. There's only a couple that have bands any more, except for some of the specials. Right?
Well, the only big band is on the Johnny Carson Show. Merv Griffin has cut his band down to a small one.
Once in a while somebody will have a special with a big band.
Yeah. Well, when he goes to Vegas he hires a big band. But other than that, it's just a small group. Everybody is trying to save money these days.
But for a while there, most of the major television shows employed a goodly number of major name Jazz musicians.

Well, for instance, all of the shows... I did Danny Kaye's show, and that had... Herb Ellis was in the rhythm section, me and Herb, and Buddy Collette happened to be on that same show. And the Jonathan Winters Show, we did that same one, and they were mostly Jazz musicians, Jazz-orientated musicians. And the Carol Burnett Show, same way. I did four years with Danny Kaye, four years with Carol Burnett (and in between that I'm doing Jonathan Winters), and four years on Flip Wilson's show. So that's twelve years of shows -- live shows, that is, with live audience.
